purpose: Separate ordinary DCP power reporting from near-zero AM/PM bypass using an already registered table with nonzero local slope around an interior zero; obtain ordinary raw V/Z/P at each new target.

input_power_identity.ordinary: Measured input power divided by the fresh zero-target control input power must match 10^(registered target dBm/10) within the registered relative tolerance. Absolute DCP input is not assumed ideal; the historical control differs from ideal by about 2.5e-8 relative.
input_power_identity.repeated_sweep: Measured input power at each registered sweep index divided by the fresh control sweep input at the same index must equal one within the registered relative tolerance.
input_power_identity.source_parameter: The run-time Pwr parameter is independently checked against its registered SI value within 1e-12 relative by the existing normalizer.
input_power_identity.baseline_input: Absolute fresh-control input DCP is compared with the historical same-configuration input DCP using the baseline power relative tolerance of 1e-7.

hypothesis_definitions.dcp_continuous: Natural cubic spline evaluated on measured ordinary DCP output dBm, added to measured ordinary source phase.
hypothesis_definitions.raw_continuous: Same spline evaluated on ordinary raw spectral output power converted to dBm; measured ordinary source phase added.
hypothesis_definitions.raw_nominal_zero_bypass: Same raw-power spline; set only its increment to zero at the registered nominal zero-dBm control, without assuming raw power is exactly 0.001 W.
hypothesis_definitions.raw_report_zero_bypass: Same raw-power spline; set its increment to zero wherever ordinary DCP output power equals exactly 0.001 W.

local_spline_polynomial.source: Analytic natural-cubic interpolation of the frozen table, not fitted to new observations.

primary_evaluation.zero_increment_test: Circular difference between measured ordinary output and input phase no greater than 1e-5 degrees.

quick_sweeps.interpretation: One same-mode baseline sweep and ten repeated control sweeps; these are not independent new model-validation points.
quick_sweeps.repeated_sweep_gate: Compare every subsequent sweep to the validated first control using registered phase/power tolerances; keep every residual and stop on a failed control before another call.

acquisition_rules: Commit this exact plan, scoring/normalization tools and frozen helper manifest before any vendor analysis.
Run the unchanged physical first-knot-negative configuration as the first ordinary/Quick Sweep reproduction control and require the complete baseline comparison to pass before new target calls.
Use independent workspace copies with exactly the registered XML field edits; form source-power expressions with Decimal arithmetic.

Every call has fresh complete ordinary raw V/Z/P, DCP and Quick Sweep data with explicit completion, empty diagnostics, 18 readbacks including Enable, exact helper/source identities, saved result workspace and closure proof.

Stop on unvalidated acquisition, failed baseline or repeated-sweep control, unexpected application/process/workspace, or missing source proof. Numerical hypothesis mismatch alone is evidence and never authorizes a rerun.
Keep at most one consecutive additional sweep endpoint separately; never count it in planned scores.
The single reserve is only for an explicitly recorded setup recovery. It cannot be spent on unexplained numerical disagreements or quiet retries.
Refresh COM variable metadata after Data/GetValue evaluation, preserve all ordered duplicate parameter occurrences, and verify restoration without another analysis.
exclusions: No parameter fitting, tolerance changes, post-hoc point selection or branch-rule changes.
The +/-1e-6 dBm points test zero versus nonzero increment; their tiny continuous-phase separation is below the phase tolerance and cannot determine an exact internal power coordinate.
Finite samples do not establish an exact reporting plateau or bypass boundary, swept raw spectra, arbitrary-table interpolation, strong compression, multitone or other frequencies.
No RFModel product formula or vendor-compatibility status changes on the basis of this preregistration.
